summary: Phase 3 Frontend Media (SmartImage + React Query) validated via Playwright on DEV preview URL. SmartImage renders with two (image/webp + image/jpeg), each exposing a srcset of 3 variants (w=400, w=800, w=1600) pointing to the Phase-2 backend image endpoints with ?w=&format= query params. Lazy loading (loading='lazy') + async decode (decoding='async') confirmed on non-priority . Mobile viewport (390x844) correctly resolves currentSrc to the w=400 variant on /galleria theme cards. Admin login no longer shows the 'Demo: admin@pompiconni.it / admin123' hint and login with credentials from backend/.env succeeds (redirects to /admin). Admin illustrations list loads and correctly falls back to gradient/emoji placeholders for the 23 illustrations that have no imageFileId (per agent-to-agent note — expected, not a bug). FIXED 1 real code bug during testing: SmartImage used the React-invalid prop name `fetchpriority` (lowercase) which emitted `Invalid DOM property fetchpriority. Did you mean fetchPriority?` console errors on every page using SmartImage — changed to `fetchPriority` (camelCase). Post-fix: 0 console errors across /, /galleria, /poster, /libri.

integration_issues.issue: /api/themes was observed to be called 4 times across the sequence /galleria -> / -> /galleria. With staleTime=5min and a shared query key ['themes'], the second /galleria visit should hit cache (0 extra calls). The hot-navigation dedupe appears imperfect — possibly because LandingPage and GalleryPage both trigger useThemes on mount and React.StrictMode is not enabled (so this isn't the usual dev double-fetch). Low severity: data still renders correctly, just more network chatter than advertised. Recommend verifying all theme consumers use queryKeys.themes and that no legacy useEffect+fetch path still exists on landing.

critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: SmartImage.jsx used `fetchpriority` (lowercase) as a JSX prop. React requires the camelCase `fetchPriority` — otherwise React logs `Invalid DOM property` errors on every render and does NOT forward the attribute to the DOM, defeating the LCP priority hint. Replaced in both the fallbackSrc branch (~L84) and the primary <picture> branch (~L119). Verified: 0 console errors post-fix across /, /galleria, /poster, /libri.

SmartImage safe-fallback ladder is correct: missing builder OR (missing idOrSlug AND missing fallbackSrc) -> neutral gray placeholder div; idOrSlug missing but fallbackSrc present -> plain ; broken flag (onError) -> pink/amber gradient div. Never produces a raw broken-image icon. Good defensive UX.

imageUrl.js correctly reads REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (no hardcoded host), encodes idOrSlug, and emits ?w=&format= query params. SUPPORTED_WIDTHS=[400,800,1600] matches the Phase-2 backend contract exactly. DEFAULT_SIZES is conservative ('(max-width: 640px) 100vw, (max-width: 1024px) 50vw, 400px').
queryClient.js: staleTime=5min, gcTime=30min, retry=1, refetchOnWindowFocus=false — sensible conservative defaults for editorial content.
App.js correctly wraps Routes in <QueryClientProvider>. CookieBanner is outside BrowserRouter but inside QueryClientProvider — correct.

AdminLogin.jsx — the 'Demo: admin@pompiconni.it / admin123' hint has been fully removed; only the placeholder inside the email <Input> remains (which is standard UX, not a credential leak). Verified visually and via innerText scan.

Minor code-quality note: SmartImage has two near-duplicate render branches (fallbackSrc path and path) with the same loading/decoding/fetchPriority logic. Could be factored into a shared render helper to prevent the fetchpriority-style typo from recurring in only one branch.

rca of the issue: SmartImage fetchpriority bug RCA: React's synthetic attribute allow-list maps JSX props to DOM attributes via a camelCase convention (fetchPriority -> fetchpriority). Using the lowercase `fetchpriority` in JSX triggers the 'Invalid DOM property' dev warning and causes React to DROP the attribute when rendering to the DOM — so the LCP priority hint was never actually set on the hero image. Reproduction: open any page containing a SmartImage and inspect the DevTools console (multiple warnings) + inspect the attributes (no fetchpriority set). Mitigation applied: replaced both occurrences in SmartImage.jsx with the React-correct `fetchPriority`. Verified post-fix: 0 console errors and the attribute now reaches the DOM.
